output.brief: The rejections trace to a data error in the new documentation suite (Tallis), not to the fungicide, Lower Serra fruit, or Meridane's equipment. The mandarin product record was copied from the avocado record on 1 Aug and kept its 7.0°C setting. Our spec is 4.0°C. Every Tallis-booked Meridane container (K3, K4, K6, K8, K9) was sent at 7.0°C and ran at 7.0°C, and each was rejected at 9–14% decay. Every container booked at 4.0°C passed. That includes K5 and K7 on the new fungicide, and the Meridane container K1. Meridane's units followed the instructions they were given, and QA's own loggers agree with the carrier downloads. A cargo claim would fail and would damage the relationship. Suspending Lower Serra growers and withholding pay would punish the wrong party. Reverting the fungicide wouldn't fix anything. Next: correct PRD-MAND-01 to 4.0°C now. Have Meridane reset the container at sea (sailed 3 Oct) and the one queued for 10 Oct. Add a pre-submission check of reefer setpoint against spec. Tell Nordhafen the cause and the fix. Confidence is high. The remaining gap is a possible smaller Lower Serra effect, which we can't separate from temperature. Independent loggers are a reasonable extra.
